item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
There is a numerical oddity on this one that completely messed up my ability to enjoy the progression, because I kept waiting for the "catch" that would make the oddity make sense. I suspect it resulted from the original choice of years being changed, but not all the references being caught.

In the last paragraph before the Research Log, it is mentioned that the second encounter was in 1965, and that the relationship was confirmed in the 1987 close approach. Neither date has an entry in the following logs, and while they are 22 years apart, they don't jive with the years that are in the logs. There is also a reference in the 2001 entry to automatic writing of "11 11 65", which is "theorized at the time to be the date of the next outbreak, and confirmed eleven years later." Um… what? These need to be corrected or verisimilitude goes out the window.

Also, Given that almost all of the words in Spanish that can be translated to create the English message at the end have multiple meanings, I would have left it in Spanish and let readers draw their own conclusions about what the message actually was and means, through either their own knowledge of Spanish or the help of Google Translate. It keeps the mysterious aspect without resorting to redaction. Based just on some quick playing around with Google Translate, there is a LOT of potential ambiguity of meaning, and it could be fun choosing the Spanish words for maximum ambiguity to keep things going.

This may seem a quibble, but it annoys me enough to downvote it, as I have a BS is Astronomy
There is no 3214 Hybris. Asteroid 3214 is named Makarenko, formerly 1978 TZ6, discovered on October 2, 1978 at Nauchnij by L. V. Zhuravleva. If your going to use an Earth-grazing asteroid, use a real one.
Also, days of the year an earth-grazing asteroid is near are all within a couple day window, not all over the seasons.

What I got from this is that there's an alien species somewhere out there that's set up a base on that asteroid. They introduce this infection for some reason (maybe to kill us? maybe to transform us into them? I don't know). The symptoms start out pretty unnoticeable, because I guess they're testing what this infection can do to us. Then, after a series of tests, they report back to whoever is their leader.
The multiples of 11 thing could really be anything. Coincidence, the aliens having an obsession about 11, the asteroid being their 11th base, all are possible.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: The main thing that really bothers me here is that you never specify what kind of contact it's transmitted by. Direct physical contact, indirect physical contact, breathing the same air, contact with bodily fluids?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
More to the point, what about the stuff that only involves 11s because we say it does? 11th floor, fine. They can count (though who knows if they would have started at 0 or 1 in floor numbering?). But understanding of geopolitical boundaries to such a refined extent (countries are arbitrary) suggests a level of closeness that ought to allow them a less absurdly convoluted method of contact.

I also really, really don't believe that the Foundation would accurately get all 11^3 people in the Quito outbreak, or that they got precise numbers for a scattered outbreak across three different countries over a year after the fact. The WHO doesn't document literally every person affected by outbreaks; they estimate. And they aren't massively burdened by the requirements of secrecy.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: All I mean with the "keeping the theme going" bit is they'd have to know the 11th most populous country, the 11th floor of a building, that some country has ~11 million people, etc. Where are they getting that targeting information?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Mathematics is a human construct; we invented and worked it to apply to our universe, so that the principles of it can be used to understand our universe more comprehensively (so, even if we prove that 1=0, nothing will actually change).

But if there's another species of intelligent life that's aware of their place in the cosmos, they probably have a parallel system, so it's not a matter of 'keeping the theme going'. They're life and sciences revolve around the number 11. They probably have another word for 11, and a system of math like our base 10. This is also kind of insightful when you think about what these aliens would be like in a social sense. They're probably very ceremonial, religious even, when it comes to 11. Just a thought. What I'm saying is, they probably have numbers too. Presumably the rest is just targeting.

You try on the lower level animals to make sure that the quirks of your 'communication disease' are all lined out. Then you move on to humans. It's how you beta test. It's responsible.

The point is, they're trying to communicate with us. It's why they started infecting more people with a higher incidence rate. They can (maybe they just do) enter close enough to us to communicate once every 11 years, and they seem to be trying to schedule and plan with us.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Well, I'm hardly in a position to complain about the fridge logic of a skip, but I do have questions.

Regarding the theme of 11: How are the aliens (or the computer on board the asteroid, or whatever it is that's generating the skip) getting the information necessary to keep the theme going? If they're pulling it from, I dunno, computer systems or whatever, then why did they need to "try" the disease on other intelligent animals before settling on humans? If they're pulling it from the humans they infect, I'm not sure they'd be able to collect the right knowledge. If they're able to "brain scan" members of our species en masse before deploying the skip, then why would it matter that the Foundation initially introduced itself as the WHO and the entity remembered (since they'd know the Foundation exists)?

Regarding the final message: Assuming it's significant that the message is 11 words, I'm not sure it cleanly translates to 11 words in Spanish. Not a Spanish expert, though.
